aiReview.summary: Official Google developer hub with API docs, reference, and pricing for Gemini, Imagen, Veo video, and Gemma open models. Strong fit as maintained official docs rather than a recap or closed landing page.
evidence: canonicalUrl https://ai.google.dev with official-web source and empty riskFlags
Excerpt lists Veo docs https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/video and API reference https://ai.google.dev/api
Excerpt lists Gemini/Imagen/Gemma docs, pricing, AI Studio, and Responsible GenAI Toolkit
uncertainty: Exact free-tier limits and current Veo API availability are not in the excerpt
SDK language coverage is not enumerated on the hub excerpt
aiReview.tagline: Official docs, APIs, and open models for builders
aiReview.description: Access official API docs, reference, and pricing for multimodal and video models, plus open-model customization and on-device guidance.
pros: Official site links Gemini, Imagen, and Veo docs, API reference, and pricing.
Includes Veo video generation docs at /gemini-api/docs/video.
Documents Gemma open models, Gemmaverse, and on-device/edge paths.
Points to Google AI Studio for model evaluation and prompting.
cons: Hub homepage is a navigation portal; implementation details live on child doc pages.
Paid API usage and quotas are not specified in the excerpt beyond a pricing link.

aiReview.summary: Official Google DeepMind Veo page covering Veo 3.1/3/2 video (and native audio) generation, with links to Gemini, Flow, a prompt guide, and Gemini API video docs. Strong fit for an AI video directory; the URL is a product/docs hub rather than a standalone SDK.
evidence: Page title and meta describe Veo 3.1 as the leading video generation model with Veo 2 capabilities.
CTA 'Build with Veo' points to https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/video.
Prompt guide at /models/veo/prompt-guide; sections include Capabilities, Performance, Safety, Showcase.
Rubric prefers official Veo docs over news recaps or closed landings without API.
uncertainty: Current commercial pricing and availability by region/account.
Exact SDK surface and rate limits without fetching the Gemini video API doc.
Whether watermarking and safety filters apply uniformly across Gemini vs Flow.
aiReview.tagline: Official video model docs with Gemini API access
aiReview.description: Official video generation model hub with native audio, prompt guidance, and links to Gemini API video docs.
pros: Official DeepMind page for Veo 3.1 with capabilities, safety, showcase, and prompt-guide sections.
Links to Gemini API video documentation for programmatic use.
Documents native audio (SFX, ambience, dialogue), prompt adherence, and physics/realism claims.
Consumer and builder paths are listed (Gemini, Google Flow, Build with Veo).
Canonical URL redirected to deepmind.google/models/veo/ and is actively maintained.
cons: Landing page is marketing-heavy; request/response API details live on a separate Gemini API doc.
Pricing, quotas, and model IDs are not specified on this page.
Candidate title still says Veo 2 / Veo 3 while the site features Veo 3.1.

aiReview.summary: Official Kuaishou video/image generation product with a documented REST API (text-to-video, image-to-video, Omni, audio). Canonical URL is a marketing app; developer docs live under /dev with prepaid API packages separate from consumer credits.
evidence: klingai.com homepage describes image/video generation, Canvas, and commercial case studies.
Developer paths such as klingai.com/dev and document-api cover text2video/image2video/omni-video and prepaid units.
Listed in awesome-video-generation as Kling AI pointing at https://klingai.com.
uncertainty: Live package prices, trial availability, and whether the newest models are on standard API packages without login.
Exact watermark and content-moderation policy on API outputs.
aiReview.tagline: Text/image-to-video API with Omni, audio, and 4K modes
aiReview.description: Generate video from text, images, and multimodal references via a prepaid REST API with polling, callbacks, and regional endpoints.
pros: Official developer docs cover authentication, async task APIs, model capability maps, and pricing units.
API supports text-to-video, image-to-video, Omni multimodal references, native audio, lip-sync, avatars, and extension.
Regional endpoints (e.g. Singapore/Beijing) and Bearer API keys are documented for production calls.
cons: The listed homepage is a consumer/marketing site; API access requires a separate prepaid resource package.
Concurrency, duration, resolution, and newest-model availability are package- and region-dependent.
No first-party full SDK is the primary path; integrations often use cURL plus polling or third-party wrappers.

aiReview.summary: Official fal-hosted HTTP API for Pika v2.2 text-to-video, with input/output schema, client examples, and per-clip pricing. Useful developer docs for a commercial inference endpoint, not an open-source model or prompt library.
evidence: llms.txt model ID fal-ai/pika/v2.2/text-to-video and POST https://fal.run/fal-ai/pika/v2.2/text-to-video
Input schema with prompt required; resolution 720p/1080p; duration 5 or 10
Output schema returns a video File URL
Candidate URL is the official API docs page linked from awesome-video-generation
uncertainty: Current uptime, queue latency, and whether v2.2 remains the latest Pika endpoint
Auth, rate limits, and commercial terms beyond the posted clip prices
HTML playground page loaded little content without JS
aiReview.tagline: Paid text-to-video inference API with client SDKs
aiReview.description: Call a 720p/1080p text-to-video endpoint via HTTP or Python/JS clients; set prompt, duration, aspect ratio, and resolution.
pros: Documents endpoint ID, HTTP URL, OpenAPI schema, and llms.txt for agents.
Lists required prompt plus optional seed, negative prompt, aspect ratio, resolution, duration, and safety checker.
Includes cURL, Python fal-client, and JavaScript @fal-ai/client subscribe examples.
States usage prices: $0.20 for 5s 720p and $0.45 for 5s 1080p.
cons: Commercial hosted inference, not an open-source model or self-hostable weights.
Duration is limited to 5 or 10 seconds in the documented schema.
Safety checker can be disabled for authorized callers, which is a policy consideration.

aiReview.summary: Artificial Analysis text-to-video leaderboard ranks T2V models by human Elo, with filters, sample counts, and API price per minute. Useful for model selection, not an SDK, API, or official model card.
evidence: Page title and meta: AA-Video-T2V v2.0 Leaderboard comparing quality, speed, and price.
Table includes Elo, samples, release dates, and API pricing footnote.
FAQ states ranking from blind pairwise human votes and links to Video Arena.
uncertainty: Whether leaderboard data is independently audited.
Exact access/paywall for full Artificial Analysis features beyond this public page.
Stability of 2026-dated model names and prices on a live board.
aiReview.tagline: Human-vote Elo rankings for text-to-video models
aiReview.description: Compare text-to-video models by blind-vote Elo, open weights, audio, and API price per minute of 1080p video.
pros: Ranks models with Elo from pairwise blind human preference votes.
Lists sample counts, release dates, and creator API pricing per minute of 1080p video.
Supports filters such as with/without audio and open weights.
Methodology is documented in FAQ (same prompt, unknown model, recruited panel).
cons: Source README labeled the link as Docs; it is a comparison site, not vendor documentation.
Not an API, SDK, or model card; rankings and prices can change and depend on AA’s panel.
Some listed models have no public API or pricing marked coming soon.

aiReview.summary: Official Runway homepage covering Creative, Dev API, and research video models. Prefer linking developers to docs.dev.runwayml.com for API details; this page is still a valid official entry point.
evidence: Excerpt lists Creative, Dev (dev.runwayml.com, docs.dev.runwayml.com), Robotics, Research, Pricing.
Claims cloud creative suite for video/image/audio and an API for developers.
Research links include Gen-4.5 and GWM-1.
riskFlags empty; source is official-web.
uncertainty: Exact API capabilities, rate limits, and current model list not in excerpt.
Open-source vs closed weights except Praxis-1 mentioned as open-weight.
Whether Dev docs are complete and maintained cannot be verified from this page alone.
aiReview.tagline: AI video, image, and audio generation plus a developer API
aiReview.description: Generate and edit video, images, and audio in a cloud suite, with a documented API for production-scale media.
pros: Official site for a major generative video lab with Creative, Dev, and research products.
Dev section points to an API platform, model list, and docs at docs.dev.runwayml.com.
Public research notes include Gen-4.5, GWM-1, and related model cards.
iOS and Android apps plus web login are listed alongside enterprise and pricing pages.
cons: The captured page is marketing copy, not SDK reference or a model card.
Pricing and API limits are not specified in the excerpt beyond try-free and enterprise offers.

aiReview.description: Connects agents to a hosted editor for cuts, captions, reframe, and MP4 export via API key. Open-source client; production runs remotely.
pros: README documents MCP install for Claude, Cursor, and related clients plus an npm package.
Client plugins and skills are MIT-licensed TypeScript with contract tests and leak-check CI.
Describes a typed edit contract and Scene IR rather than one-shot locked pixels.
cons: Four stars, zero forks, and no issues; maintenance and production reliability are unproven.
Heavy lifting is a closed hosted GPU API requiring livecore.ai keys and credits.
Targets editing/export, not maintained video-generation model cards or official Veo/Runway docs.
